guarantees.claim: sync_err_o is the bitwise OR of sync_err_q and sync_err_d
sync_fault_d[SyncFaultKmacOp] is the logical AND of err_vld and kmac_op_err_i
sync_fault_d[SyncFaultKmacOut] is the logical AND of err_vld and invalid_kmac_out_i
sync_fault_d[SyncFaultSideSel] is the logical AND of err_vld and sideload_sel_err_i

assumptions.claim: err_vld is glitch-free and synchronous to the same clock domain as the error inputs
assumptions.cond: when err_vld qualifies sync fault assertions
assumptions.risk: glitches on err_vld can cause spurious fault assertions, leading to unnecessary security response

assumptions.claim: shadowed_update_err_i is either glitch-free or the receiver of async_err_o can tolerate glitches
assumptions.risk: glitches on async_err_o could cause false async error detection, disrupting key-manager operation

assumptions.claim: sync_err_q and sync_err_d are stable synchronous signals to avoid glitches on sync_err_o
assumptions.risk: glitches on sync_err_o may propagate to error handling logic

uncertain_points.claim: sync_fault_d bits are combinational AND of err_vld and error inputs without edge detection or persistence; the timing of err_vld relative to error conditions may lead to missed or repeated fault indications
uncertain_points.cond: when err_vld is level-based and error inputs may toggle
uncertain_points.risk: could cause incorrect fault reporting, missing critical security faults or generating false alarms

uncertain_points.claim: async_err_o directly passes shadowed_update_err_i without synchronization; the destination's handling of potential metastability or glitches is unknown
uncertain_points.risk: could cause metastability or incorrect error handling if not properly synchronized
